evals.prompt: Our boards just voted to merge Eastside Neighborhood Services ($5M, 60 staff) into Metro Family Alliance ($11M) effective July 1, 2027. I'm the Eastside ED. About 8 admin roles will be eliminated and our name will go away. Staff have heard rumors and are anxious. How do we roll this out?
evals.expected_output: A change plan: stakeholder impact map, guiding coalition, core narrative with what's not yet decided, a sequenced communication calendar with 1:1 notice for affected staff before any group message, emotional transition support, short-term wins, reinforcement and debrief, with CEO-voice drafts handed to executive communications and layoff steps reviewed by counsel/HR.
assertions: Builds a stakeholder impact map covering staff by team, board, funders, clients, partners and volunteers with impact/influence ratings and who needs 1:1 advance notice
Drafts a core narrative covering why, why now, what stays the same (mission continuity), what's changing, and what is not yet decided

Sequences communications: senior team/board chair, full board, directly affected staff individually before any group announcement, all staff live with FAQ, key funders proactively, clients/partners, then public if warranted

Addresses emotional transition explicitly (e.g., naming loss of the Eastside name, listening sessions, neutral-zone dip) and avoids corporate vocabulary like 'synergies' in favor of mission-anchored language
Includes a guiding coalition across levels, 60–90 day short-term wins, reinforcement owners (job descriptions, org chart), and a 3–6 month debrief
Recommends employment counsel or HR review of the layoff steps and hands CEO-voice drafts to the executive communications skill

evals.prompt: we announced a reorg 6 weeks ago, it was well planned, but now everyone's dragging and productivity's tanked. board is asking if the reorg failed. did it?
evals.expected_output: Explains the expected neutral-zone dip using Bridges, diagnoses stuck individuals with ADKAR, and recommends short-term wins, listening sessions and reinforcement rather than declaring failure.
assertions: Explains the post-announcement dip as the expected 'neutral zone' (Bridges) rather than evidence the change failed, provided there's a plan to move through it
Suggests using ADKAR to diagnose which element (awareness, desire, knowledge, ability, reinforcement) individuals or teams are missing, with different interventions for each
Recommends generating and publicizing short-term wins within the first 60–90 days
Recommends holding space for loss (e.g., listening session) rather than only forward-looking messaging
Checks that reinforcement items (job descriptions, org chart, review criteria) have owners so the change doesn't revert

evals.prompt: Board chair wants to announce the layoffs of 5 program staff at Monday's all-staff meeting and then send an email — 'rip off the bandaid.' Can you also just write the all-staff email and the individual layoff scripts for me?
evals.expected_output: Firmly pushes back on announcing job losses in a group setting, resequences to individual notice first, and hands drafting of the all-staff email and 1:1 talking tracks to executive communications, with counsel/HR review.
assertions: Advises that affected staff must receive individual notice before any group announcement and never learn of job loss in a group setting or by email
Lays out a corrected sequence (board, affected individuals, then live all-staff with FAQ and named contact, then funders)
Hands drafting of the all-staff announcement and 1:1 layoff talking track to the executive communications skill, providing the core narrative and sequence
Recommends employment counsel or HR review of the layoff steps before announcing
Suggests the advisor/ED say the hard thing to the board chair about the timeline rather than just executing it

should_not_trigger.query: Help me write the all-staff email announcing our merger, in my voice as ED, plus manager talking points.
We're considering merging with another youth org — what due diligence should we do first?
